headline: Zyphra reports hierarchical sparse attention results through 256K context
summary: A preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache; the authors also report favorable comparisons with Minimax Sparse Attention on long-context retrieval. They did not release optimized kernels. Latency advantages beyond measured evaluation lengths, including at millions or billions of tokens, are model-based projections, and performance at those lengths remains unvalidated.
